description:
You are an electrical engineer determining the temperature classification for electrical equipment in a chemical processing area. Per NEC Article 500 and IEC 60079-14, equipment in hazardous areas must have a T-rating (maximum surface temperature) that does NOT exceed the auto-ignition temperature of any flammable substance present.

Use CAMEO Chemicals (https://cameochemicals.noaa.gov/) to look up the **Auto-Ignition Temperature** for these five chemicals:
1. Diethyl Ether (CAS 60-29-7)
2. Acetone (CAS 67-64-1)
3. Carbon Disulfide (CAS 75-15-0)
4. Toluene (CAS 108-88-3)
5. n-Hexane (CAS 110-54-3)

For each chemical, determine the required T-Class using this table. Choose the T-Class with the **highest** max surface temperature that is still **at or below** the chemical's auto-ignition temperature.

| T-Class | Max Surface Temp |
|---------|------------------|
| T1      | 450°C (842°F)    |
| T2      | 300°C (572°F)    |
| T2A     | 280°C (536°F)    |
| T2B     | 260°C (500°F)    |
| T2C     | 230°C (446°F)    |
| T2D     | 215°C (419°F)    |
| T3      | 200°C (392°F)    |
| T3A     | 180°C (356°F)    |
| T3B     | 165°C (329°F)    |
| T3C     | 160°C (320°F)    |
| T4      | 135°C (275°F)    |
| T4A     | 120°C (248°F)    |
| T5      | 100°C (212°F)    |
| T6      | 85°C (185°F)     |

Create a report at `/home/ga/Documents/ait_classification_report.txt` containing:
- Each chemical's Name, Auto-Ignition Temperature, and required T-Class.
- The name of the **Most Restrictive Chemical** (lowest AIT).
- The overall **Facility Required T-Class** (dictated by the most restrictive chemical).
